learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with the basic knowledge of chemistry essential to form a scientific knowledge to which to add the specific characteristics of the course of study. In particular, the course topics are selected in such a way as to enable students to face, understand and evaluate the chemical, thermodynamic, kinetic and catalytic aspects related to chemical processes and their optimal conduction.

Knowledge of the laws of chemistry and some laws of physics (thermodynamics) relevant to industrial engineering, together with an understanding of their role in formulating models that represent physical reality.

Ability to apply knowledge of chemistry to solve disciplinary problems in chemistry, applied chemistry and theoretical thermodynamics, interpreting and applying the governing physical laws in subsequent engineering applications.
Ability to analyse data and information using established methods and tools, interpret results, and draw consistent conclusions, also with the support of provided guidance.

Ability to organize one's work while meeting assigned deadlines, managing available time and resources effectively, realistically assessing one's own capabilities, and contributing to task prioritization.
Ability to recognize personal knowledge limitations and the need to acquire new competencies by identifying appropriate information sources and guided learning opportunities.
Ability to present engineering problems, solutions, analyses, and results clearly and systematically through written reports and oral presentations, following standard formats and conventions.

Ability to graphically represent and communicate technical data, results, and engineering solutions through the preparation of drawings, diagrams, graphs, and tables, using established tools and conventions.

Ability to identify and consult bibliographic sources and technical documentation through the main available resources (libraries, databases, technical manuals, and digital resources), selecting relevant information with appropriate guidance.

syllabus_topics: The electronic structure of atoms and the chemical periodicity
Intermolecular forces and states of matter
Isotopes, atomic weight, molecular weight, mole
The quantum-mechanical model of the atom
Periodic table of the elements and periodic quantities
Polar covalent bonds and dipole moment
General characteristics of metals and metallic bonding (gas theory and band theory)
Intermolecular forces and states of aggregation of matter
Types of solids: metallic, ionic, covalent and molecular
Main properties of the different types of solids
Gas mixtures (partial pressures and Dalton law)
Standard reduction potential and the Nernst equation
Spontaneity and displacement of redox reactions
assessment_rules: The assessment includes a written exam followed by an oral exam, reserved for students who pass the written exam. The written test verifies the ability to apply acquired knowledge to solve chemical problems. The oral exam covers corrections from the written exam and knowledge of course topics relevant to industrial engineering. The final assessment considers both exam results, as well as independent judgment, communication, and learning skills. Grading ranges from Fail (Insufficient) to 29-30 and Honors (Excellent or Outstanding), based on conceptual understanding, application ability, independence, and critical thinking.
